# ankra_aws_role_credential (Resource)

An AWS credential the platform uses by assuming an IAM role. Create the role with the trust policy `ankra credentials aws onboarding` prints, using the same external id. The counterpart of `ankra credentials aws create-role` and `ankra credentials delete`.

**Changes.** Changing `role_arn` or `external_id` rotates the secret in place: the platform checks the new value with the provider and stores it only when the provider accepts it, otherwise the apply fails and the credential keeps its secret. `display_name` also changes in place. The other settings identify what the credential connects to, so changing them replaces the credential.

**Drift.** The platform never returns a secret, so a secret changed outside Terraform is not detected; the name, the display name and the credential's existence are, and so are `region` and `scope`. A platform from before 2026-10-18 does not list these settings, and a setting the platform could not read is not listed; either way the value in state is kept rather than reported as changed.

**Permissions.** The API token needs `credentials.read` as well as `credentials.write` (and `credentials.delete` to destroy): the provider reads the credential listing right after a create to fill in the read-only attributes. If that read fails, the credential is kept in state and marked tainted, so run `terraform untaint` to keep it. (A platform from before 2026-10-18 does not answer a create with the credential's id; there the error names the `terraform import` to run.)

**Projects.** A credential belongs to the provider's project. After the provider's `project_id` changes, a credential from the old project is reported as not visible in the current scope; it is neither recreated nor reported destroyed.

**Refresh cost.** Every refresh reads the credential listing for this provider. For AWS credentials the platform reads each AWS credential's secret to fill in `scope` and `auth_method`, so a refresh costs one secret read per AWS credential in the organisation.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ankra_aws_role_credential" "provisioning" {
  name        = "aws-provisioning"
  role_arn    = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ankra-provisioning"
  external_id = var.aws_external_id
  scope       = "provisioning"
  region      = "eu-north-1"
}

# The external id the role's trust policy requires, as printed by
# `ankra credentials aws onboarding --scope provisioning`.
variable "aws_external_id" {
  type = string
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `external_id` (String) External id the role's trust policy requires. Changing it rotates the credential in place.
- `name` (String) Credential name, unique per provider in the organisation. Changing it replaces the credential.
- `role_arn` (String) ARN of the IAM role the platform assumes. Changing it rotates the credential in place.

### Optional

- `display_name` (String) Label shown instead of the name in the Ankra portal. Changed in place. Left unset, the label set in the portal (if any) is kept and read back; removing it from the configuration does not clear it.
- `region` (String) Default AWS region. Defaults to `us-east-1`. Changing it replaces the credential. A change made outside Terraform shows as drift.
- `scope` (String) Scope the role was onboarded under: `cost`, `provisioning` or `self_managed`. Defaults to `cost`. Changing it replaces the credential. A change made outside Terraform shows as drift.

### Read-Only

- `available` (Boolean) Whether the platform considers the credential usable.
- `created_at` (String) When the credential was created.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the credential: the value cluster resources take as `credential_id` or `ssh_key_credential_id`.
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state the platform reports, such as `up`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Credentials are imported by id. The platform never returns a credential's secrets,
# so the first apply after an import adopts the configured values without replacing it.
terraform import ankra_aws_role_credential.provisioning 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
```
